examples.en: My father is a reserve army colonel.
My brother was discharged last year, so he is in the reserves now.

examples.ko: 예비역 모임에서 오랜만에 옛 전우들을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met my old comrades after a long time at the reservists' gathering.

examples.ko: 예비역 장교들이 학교에서 안보 강연을 했어요.
examples.en: Reserve officers gave a talk on national security at the school.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 예비역이라서 예비군 훈련 때문에 이틀 동안 휴가를 냈어요.
examples.en: My uncle is a reservist, so he took two days off for his reserve training.

examples.ko: 예비역이 되면 일 년에 한두 번 훈련을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Once you become a reservist, you have to take part in training once or twice a year.

explain: 반의어는 '현역'이에요. '예비역 대령'처럼 계급 앞에 붙이거나 '예비역이에요'처럼 신분을 말할 때 써요. 예비역이 받는 훈련은 '예비군 훈련'이라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I finished my military service and became a reservist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전역한 뒤에 신분이 바뀐다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the change in status after being discharged.

phrases.example: 오늘 예비군 훈련이 있어서 회사에 못 가요.
phrases.en: I can't go to work today because I have reserve training.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예비역이 받는 훈련을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common term for the training reservists attend.

phrases.en: My uncle is a reserve soldier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군인이었다가 지금은 예비 신분인 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who was a soldier and now holds reserve status.

explain_en: Military — status or person after finishing active service. The opposite is '현역' (active duty). It goes before a rank, as in '예비역 대령', or states someone's status, as in '예비역이에요'. The training reservists receive is often called '예비군 훈련'.

examples.ko: 교통 법규 위반자는 벌금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: Traffic law violators have to pay a fine.
The police are looking for the rule violator.
A notice is stuck on the car of the parking violator.
I heard they stepped up enforcement because violators kept increasing.
The list of violators was posted online.

examples.ko: 마스크 규정 위반자는 입장할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Those who violate the mask rule cannot enter.

explain: 주로 법, 규칙, 규정을 어긴 사람을 가리킬 때 써요. '교통 법규 위반자'처럼 앞에 어긴 내용을 붙이는 경우가 많고, 뉴스나 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '규칙을 어긴 사람'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: People who break the rules get punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '위반자' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 위반자.

phrases.en: The name of the rule violator was posted on the board.
phrases.nuance_ko: '규칙'을 앞에 붙여 무엇을 어겼는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting 규칙 in front says what was violated.

phrases.en: Violators have to pay a fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 법을 어긴 사람이 받는 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the consequence for someone who broke a rule or law.

explain_en: It is used for a person who broke a law, rule or regulation. It often comes with what was broken, like '교통 법규 위반자', and you see it in news and notices. In daily talk people also say '규칙을 어긴 사람'.

en: to break the law; to infringe the law

examples.en: That action is illegal by law.
I heard the company made money in an illegal way.
The lawyer said this contract is illegal.
The police are cracking down on illegal parking.

examples.ko: 몰래 찍은 영상이 위법할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A video taken secretly can be illegal.
The ad was taken down right away because it was illegal.

explain: '위법하다'는 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '불법이다'가 더 흔하고, '위법'은 법의 규칙을 어겼다는 점을 따질 때 어울려요. '위법을 하다'보다 '위법한 행동'처럼 꾸미는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That is clearly an illegal act.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 '위법한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 위법한 to modify a following noun.

phrases.en: This method is not against the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법을 어기지 않았다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something doesn't break the law.

phrases.en: Parking on the street is illegal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '불법'이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, 불법 is more common.

explain_en: 위법하다 appears mostly in news and legal talk. In daily life 불법이다 is more common, while 위법 fits when you discuss whether a legal rule was broken. It often shows up as a modifier, like 위법한 행동.

examples.en: The government approved the founding of the new school.

examples.ko: 교육청이 이 학원을 정식으로 인가하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The education office decided to officially approve this institute.

examples.ko: 인가하지 않은 업체는 영업할 수 없어요.
examples.en: A business that has not been authorized cannot operate.

examples.ko: 시청에서 인가한 행사만 광장에서 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only events authorized by city hall can be held in the square.
Once the committee approves the plan, construction starts.

examples.ko: 담당 부서가 곧 사업을 인가할 거라고 했어요.
examples.en: The department in charge said it will approve the project soon.

explain: '허락하다'는 누구에게나 쓰지만 '인가하다'는 국가나 관청이 공식으로 인정해 줄 때 써요. 학교·학원·병원·단체 이야기에서 자주 보여요. 주어가 보통 정부나 관청이에요.

phrases.en: The education office approved the academy's establishment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관청이 허락을 해 준다는 느낌이 분명해요. 주어는 보통 정부나 관청이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clearly conveys an authority granting permission; the subject is usually a government body.

phrases.en: The government did not authorize that organization.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락해 주지 않았다고 말할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 이런 형태를 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say official permission was not given; this form is common in news.

phrases.en: The committee approved the new plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인가하다'와 비슷하지만 계획이나 신청처럼 더 넓은 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 인가하다 but used more broadly, such as for plans or applications.

explain_en: '허락하다' works between anyone, but '인가하다' is used when a state or public office gives official approval. It often appears with schools, institutes, hospitals, and organizations, and the subject is usually the government or an office.

dis.h: authority grants permission or a license
gh: officially recognize as valid or qualified

p.n: 공인하다 does not fit with 'permitting the founding of a school'; it means recognizing something as official or valid.

t90.ax: The government approved the founding of the new school.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 저작물이라서 허락 없이 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This photo is a copyrighted work, so you can't use it without permission.

examples.ko: 다른 사람의 저작물을 쓸 때는 출처를 꼭 밝히세요.
examples.en: When you use someone else's work, be sure to give the source.
My work was spread around the internet without permission.

examples.ko: 저작물 이용 허락을 받으려고 출판사에 메일을 보냈어요.
examples.en: I emailed the publisher to get permission to use the work.
The creator holds the rights to a work.

examples.ko: 음악, 영화, 책은 모두 저작물에 들어가요.
examples.en: Music, films and books all count as creative works.

explain: 책, 음악, 그림, 사진처럼 사람이 만든 창작물을 법적으로 부르는 말이에요. '저작권', '저작물 이용'처럼 법이나 계약 이야기에서 써요. 일상에서는 '작품'이 더 가볍게 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 저작물을 이용하려면 먼저 허락을 받아야 해요.
phrases.en: To use a copyrighted work, you must get permission first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법이나 계약에서 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation used in law and contracts.

phrases.example: 노래는 저작권이 있어서 허락 없이 영상에 쓰면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Songs are copyrighted, so you can't use them in videos without permission.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저작물을 만든 사람이 가지는 권리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The rights held by the person who made the work.

phrases.example: 이 작품은 제가 직접 그린 그림이에요.
phrases.en: This work is a picture I drew myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '저작물'보다 '작품'이 더 가볍고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 작품 sounds lighter and more natural than 저작물.

explain_en: Legal/formal term for any work protected by copyright. It is the legal term for things people create, such as books, music, pictures and photos. It appears in legal and contract talk, as in '저작권' (copyright) and '저작물 이용' (use of a work). In daily speech '작품' feels lighter.

dis.h: a creative work protected by copyright

p.n: 저작 is more about the writing or authorship than the legal object.

examples.en: This transaction is completely legal.
They made the arrest through lawful procedures.
I asked a lawyer whether that method is legal.

examples.ko: 허가 없이 찍은 사진은 적법하지 않아요.
examples.en: Photos taken without permission are not lawful.
If it had been legal, it wouldn't have been a problem.
The money was earned legally, so I'm not worried.

explain: 적법하다는 뉴스, 재판, 계약서처럼 딱딱한 자리에서 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '합법이에요'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '위법하다'예요. '적법한 절차', '적법하게'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 형태로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That company earned its money legally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form is used to describe how an action is done.

phrases.en: This method is legal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It has a similar meaning and sounds more natural in daily speech.

phrases.example: 허가 없이 집을 짓는 건 적법하지 않아요.
phrases.en: Building a house without a permit is not legal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법에 맞지 않을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This negative form says something does not follow the law.

explain_en: 적법하다 is used mostly in formal settings such as news, trials, and contracts. In daily talk, 합법이에요 sounds more natural. The opposite is 위법하다. It often appears in forms that modify what follows, like 적법한 절차 and 적법하게.

examples.ko: 불법 점유는 처벌을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Illegal occupation can be punished.

examples.ko: 회의실 점유 시간을 한 시간으로 정했어요.
examples.en: We set the meeting room occupancy time to one hour.

examples.ko: 가게 앞 인도 점유 때문에 불편하다는 민원이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many complaints that the shop's use of the sidewalk is inconvenient.

examples.ko: 사무실 점유 기간이 이번 달 말까지예요.
examples.en: The office occupancy period runs through the end of this month.

examples.ko: 점유와 소유는 다르다고 법 수업에서 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned in law class that possession and ownership are different.

examples.ko: 그 땅의 점유가 누구에게 있는지 아직 몰라요.
examples.en: I still don't know who is in possession of that land.

explain: 점유는 실제로 차지해서 쓰고 있는 상태, 소유는 법적으로 내 것인 상태예요. 세 들어 사는 집은 점유는 해도 소유는 아니에요. 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 일상에서는 '차지'라는 말을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 이 회사는 휴대폰 시장 점유율이 높아요.
phrases.en: This company has a high share of the mobile phone market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점유율은 시장이나 전체에서 차지하는 비율을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 점유율 is used for the percentage something holds in a market or a whole.

phrases.example: 남의 땅을 무단 점유하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not occupy someone else's land without permission.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락 없이 차지한다는 뜻이라서 뉴스와 법 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means occupying something without permission, and it often appears in news and legal talk.

phrases.example: 큰 책상이 방의 반을 점유하고 있어요.
phrases.en: A big desk takes up half of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '점유'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사로, 어떤 곳을 차지해서 쓴다는 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '차지하다'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '점유', meaning to take up and use a place. In everyday talk people say '차지하다' more often.

explain_en: Legal/formal — occupying a space or place, not owning it (도로 점유) 점유 is actually holding and using something; 소유 (ownership) is legally owning it. A rented home is in your 점유 but not your 소유. It appears mostly in news and legal talk; in daily speech Koreans lean on 차지 (taking up a space).

p.n: 점거 implies forcible seizure, so it does not fit simply taking up seats.

examples.en: The government decided to make remote work an official system.
Waste decreased after recycling separation was made an official system.

examples.ko: 이 규칙을 제도화하면 모두가 따르기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If we make this rule official, it will be easy for everyone to follow.
The company made parental leave an official system last year.

examples.ko: 좋은 관행을 제도화한 뒤에도 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Problems can still arise after a good practice has been formalized.

examples.ko: 학교에서 이 활동을 제도화하자는 의견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Opinions came up to make this activity an official program at school.

explain: 관행이나 약속을 법이나 규칙 같은 공식적인 틀로 만든다는 점에서 '정해 두다'보다 훨씬 무게가 있어요. 보통 '~을/를 제도화하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 일이 저절로 그렇게 되었을 때는 '제도화되다'를 써요. 뉴스나 보고서에서 자주 보는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Parental leave was made into an official system, so it's easier to use.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제도화하다'와 달리 누가 만들었는지보다 공식 제도가 된 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 제도화하다, it focuses on the result of becoming an official system rather than who did it.

phrases.en: We need to make safety education an official system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 필요하다는 의견을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state an opinion that it is necessary.

phrases.en: The government institutionalized that policy by law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 방식으로 공식화하는지 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say by what means something is made official.

explain_en: It carries much more weight than simply '정해 두다' because it turns a practice or agreement into an official framework like a law or rule. It is usually used as '~을/를 제도화하다', and when things become that way on their own you use '제도화되다'. You often see it in news and reports.

en: to sanction; to restrain; to restrict

examples.en: The government decided to crack down on illegal ads.
The school took disciplinary action against a student who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 여러 나라가 그 나라를 제재한 뒤 무역이 줄었어요.
examples.en: After several countries imposed sanctions, trade decreased.
Extreme behavior has to be restricted.

examples.ko: 나쁜 말을 쓴 사용자를 제재하는 규칙이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A rule was made to penalize users who use abusive language.

examples.ko: 협회가 선수를 제재하면 경기에 나갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the association sanctions a player, they can't play in games.

explain: 규칙이나 법을 어긴 사람, 회사, 나라에게 불이익을 주어 활동을 막거나 제한할 때 써요. '벌하다'는 벌 자체에 초점이 있어요. 뉴스에서는 '경제 제재'로 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 법을 어겨서 제재를 받았어요.
phrases.en: That company was sanctioned for breaking the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제재를 당하는 쪽의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the one being sanctioned.

phrases.en: The government imposed sanctions on that country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제재하는 쪽이 불이익을 주는 행동을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the acting side imposes a penalty.

phrases.example: 경제 제재 때문에 물건값이 많이 올랐어요.
phrases.en: Prices rose a lot because of the economic sanctions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 들리는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun collocation you hear most often in the news.

explain_en: Restrain or penalize an action by rule or authority. Use it when you penalize a person, company, or country that broke rules or laws by limiting or blocking their activity. '벌하다' focuses on punishment itself. In the news you often hear it in '경제 제재' (economic sanctions).

t90.ax: Extreme behavior has to be restricted.

examples.en: The school limits phone use.
The doctor limited how much salt I eat.

examples.ko: 이 길은 큰 차의 진입을 제한하고 있어요.
examples.en: This road restricts entry for large vehicles.

examples.ko: 나이를 제한한 행사라서 저는 못 가요.
examples.en: It is an age-restricted event, so I cannot go.
We take the test with a time limit.
From now on I will limit my game time.

explain: 사람이나 규칙이 양, 시간, 대상에 한계를 정할 때 써요. 명사 '제한'은 '시간 제한', '나이 제한'처럼 자주 써요. 스스로 줄이는 것은 '줄이다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Admission to this movie is restricted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 제한하는지 말하지 않고 한계가 있다는 사실만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: States that a limit exists without saying who set it.

phrases.en: The restaurant puts a limit on meal time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙으로 한계를 만든다는 뜻으로 '제한하다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means setting a limit by rule, similar to '제한하다'.

phrases.example: 이 앱은 사용 시간을 제한하지 않아요.
phrases.en: This app doesn't limit usage time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한계가 없다고 안내할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used in notices saying there is no limit.

explain_en: Someone sets a cap or restriction by rule (게임 시간을 제한하다) It is used when a person or rule sets a ceiling on an amount, a time or who may take part. The noun '제한' is common in '시간 제한' and '나이 제한'. When you cut back by yourself, '줄이다' also works.

en: to base; to be based on

examples.ko: 이 보고서는 국제 기준에 준거해 작성했어요.
examples.en: This report was written based on international standards.

examples.ko: 심사는 공개된 평가 기준에 준거하여 진행돼요.
examples.en: The screening is carried out in accordance with the published criteria.

examples.ko: 법에 준거하지 않은 계약은 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A contract that does not conform to the law can become a problem.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 업계 표준에 준거한 방식으로 일해요.
examples.en: Our company works in a way that follows industry standards.

examples.ko: 어떤 자료에 준거했는지 출처를 밝혀 주세요.
examples.en: Please state your source and which materials you based this on.
The person in charge explained that it was handled according to the regulations.

explain: 거의 '~에 준거하여/준거해'의 모양으로 쓰고, '~에 따라'를 딱딱하게 말한 느낌이에요. 보고서, 법, 논문에서 주로 보이고 일상 대화에서는 '~에 따라', '~대로'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I will handle it in accordance with the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문서나 공식적인 말에서 '~에 따라'의 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way of saying 'in accordance with' in documents or official talk.

phrases.example: 이 점수는 학교 기준에 준거한 결과예요.
phrases.en: This score is a result based on the school's standards.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸며서 어떤 기준에 바탕을 둔 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for results that are based on a standard.

phrases.en: Please submit the application according to the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '준거하여' 대신 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more common everyday replacement for '준거하여'.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '~에 준거하여/준거해', a stiff version of '~에 따라'. You mostly see it in reports, laws, and papers, while in daily talk people say '~에 따라' or '~대로'.

examples.en: This street is designated as a no-smoking zone.
My seat has already been assigned.
Please come at the designated time.
That building was designated a cultural heritage site.
I'll let you know once a person in charge is assigned.

examples.ko: 주차는 지정되어 있는 곳에만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only park in designated spots.

explain: 사람이 아니라 장소, 시간, 자리가 주어로 '정해진다'는 뜻이에요. '지정석'(정해진 자리), '지정 장소'처럼 명사 앞에 붙는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 '정해지다'보다 공식적으로 정해졌다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 기차표는 지정석이라서 자리를 고를 수 없어요.
phrases.en: This train ticket is for a reserved seat, so I can't choose my seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 정해진 자리를 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for a seat that has been set in advance.

phrases.example: 지정된 장소에서만 담배를 피울 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can only smoke in the designated area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: The parking area hasn't been designated yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 정해지지 않았다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it hasn't been set yet.

explain_en: Passive — something is set in advance (seats, areas, items) The subject is a place, time, or seat that gets officially set. It often attaches to nouns, as in 지정석 (assigned seat) and 지정 장소. Compared with the plain 정해지다, it sounds more official.

examples.en: The mayor handled the matter on his own authority of office.
A judge must not abuse his authority.
This is outside my authority.
The chairperson called the meeting on the authority of the post.

examples.ko: 경찰관이 직권을 이용해 개인 정보를 봤다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was news that a police officer used his authority to look at personal information.

examples.ko: 공무원은 자기 직권 안에서만 일을 결정할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A public official can decide matters only within his own authority.

explain: 직무에 따라 주어지는 권한이에요. '직권으로'는 누가 신청하지 않아도 담당자가 스스로 판단해서 한다는 뜻으로 뉴스와 공문서에 자주 나와요. '직권 남용'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 일반적인 '권한'보다 직책에 묶인 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: An official's abuse of authority was in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맡은 권한을 잘못 쓴다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 아주 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means misusing one's granted power; very common in the news.

phrases.en: The principal decided on his own authority to close the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신청이 없어도 담당자가 스스로 결정한다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the person in charge decides without anyone asking.
phrases.en_equiv: to decide on one's own authority

phrases.en: This matter falls under the mayor's authority.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 직책이 가진 권한 안의 일이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the matter lies within the power of that position.

explain_en: Power that comes with an official post, used without asking others. It is the power that comes with a job or post. '직권으로' means the person in charge acts on their own judgment without anyone applying, and it often appears in news and official documents. '직권 남용' is also a common phrase. It is tied to a position more strongly than the general word '권한'.

examples.en: City Hall carries out this year's budget.
The police enforced the law fairly.

examples.ko: 회사는 다음 달부터 광고비를 집행할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will start spending its ad budget next month.
We record where all the money being spent goes.
After carrying out the plan, we checked the results.

examples.ko: 판결을 그대로 집행한 뒤 사건이 끝났어요.
examples.en: After the ruling was carried out as it was, the case ended.

explain: 정해 둔 계획, 법, 예산을 권한이 있는 곳이 실제로 실행할 때 써요. '실행하다'는 누구나 하는 일에 쓰지만 '집행하다'는 정부, 회사, 법원 같은 공식적인 곳에서 주로 해요. 뉴스와 공문서에는 많이 나오고 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.

phrases.en: This year's budget has all been spent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집행하는 쪽이 아니라 실행된 것이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the subject is the thing that gets carried out, not the one carrying it out.

phrases.en: Law enforcement must be fair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법을 실제로 지키게 하는 일을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for actually enforcing the law.

phrases.en: I carry out my plans right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집행하다'보다 쉽고 누구나 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 'jiphaenghada' and usable by anyone.

explain_en: Official; laws, budgets, sentences carried out by authorities. Used when an authorized body actually carries out a set plan, law or budget. '실행하다' is for anyone, but '집행하다' mostly belongs to governments, companies and courts. It is common in news and official documents and rare in everyday talk.

dis.h: carry out laws, budgets, or sentences
gh: carry out a task or duty
boldly carry out a drastic measure

p.n: 실시하다 does not combine naturally with a budget.

t90.ax: The police enforced the law fairly.
